clue.text: Reflect about one's bad treatment

indicators.note: the verb for reflecting is placed around the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: to reflect is to muse
one is I, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone thinks back on how badly they were treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse is ill-treatment or abuse, the noun sense of handling something wrongly.

clue.text: Chap clutching part of face, say, beginning to unmask serial killer

indicators.note: the word for chap grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man
the chin is part of the face
say means for example, EG

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word unmask is taken

explanation.surface: A man with a hidden face is unmasked as a serial killer.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN holds CHIN, EG and U: MA + CHIN EG U + N.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine gun fires bullets in rapid series, a witty kind of serial killer.

clue.text: Fish spawn round river

indicators.note: the word for spawn goes round the letter for river

parts.note: spat is the spawn of shellfish such as oysters

explanation.surface: Fish lay spawn around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Odds on school sacking head, a British resident

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at a race's start

indicators.note: the first letter of the school's name is dismissed

parts.note: Harrow is an English public school

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds on a school dismissing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price in horse racing. HARROW loses H to give ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a bird found living all over Britain, so a resident rather than a migrant.

clue.text: Make criticism about hosts dropping one: that grates

indicators.note: the word for criticising goes around the reduced word for hosts

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: the word for hosts lets go of the letter standing for one

parts.note: hosts are armies, great multitudes
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a party's hosts after one guest drops out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' looks like people entertaining guests, but here it means armies, an older sense of a great multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese usually grated over food, so it is something that grates.

clue.text: Very musical, at heart of old Christmas festivities

indicators.note: only the core of the word is kept, losing its first and last letters

parts.note: wassail is old Christmas merrymaking with spiced ale

explanation.surface: Something very musical at the heart of old Christmas revels.
explanation.walkthrough: WASSAIL without its first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian term in music meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Craze to possess house plant

indicators.note: the word for craze holds the abbreviation for house

parts.note: a mania is a craze

explanation.surface: A craze for owning a house plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahonia is an evergreen shrub with yellow flowers, a garden plant.

clue.text: Simon for one limps badly to school

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, so rearranged

parts.note: Eton is an English public school

explanation.surface: A boy named Simon limps on his way to school.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Simple Simon' makes Simon the classic simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme is an example of a foolish person.

clue.text: One hunted fittingly lost head in grass

indicators.note: the first letter of the creature's name is removed

parts.note: Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark is told in 'fits'

explanation.surface: A hunted animal loses its head in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Carroll's poem divides into 'fits', hence 'fittingly'. 'Grass' is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark is slang for an informer, as is grass.

clue.text: Person making too much effort, one with crossed wires?

definitions.meaning: a sieve's mesh of criss-crossed wires

explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is one who strains, and also a sieve made of woven wire mesh.

clue.text: Shakespeare's undoubtedly holding the lead as writer

indicators.note: the archaic word for certainly holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: certes is an old word for certainly, used by Shakespeare
the van is the leading part, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A claim that Shakespeare is surely the foremost writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic 'certes' turns up in Shakespeare's plays; 'the lead' suggests the front of a column, the vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, is a famous Spanish writer.

clue.text: Poet's beginning to recite at institution

parts.note: a home is an institution such as a care home

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word recite is taken

explanation.surface: A poet starts reciting at some institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Poet's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: See Lenin tear into a revolutionary hymn

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching Lenin tear into a revolutionary song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges LENIN TEAR INTO A; 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Internationale is the socialist anthem, a hymn of the workers' movement.

clue.text: Acted, alienating millions for a time: it's easy to pull off

indicators.note: the letter for millions is pushed out and replaced

parts.note: performed means acted
A plus T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor drops millions for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' says what replaces M in PERFORMED: A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perforated has a line of holes so it tears off easily.

clue.text: Provide funds, enough to get daughter settled

indicators.note: the daughter is settled into the word for enough, sitting inside it

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: Parents give enough money for their daughter to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: ENOW is an old poetic word for 'enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a person or institution a permanent income or funding.

clue.text: Crude hand working here out West?

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough labourer working on an American ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude ranch is a holiday ranch in the American West where tourists play cowboy.

clue.text: What underpromotion on board may get you in City?

definitions.text: What underpromotion on board may get you
definitions.meaning: in chess, promoting a pawn to a rook instead of a queen gives a fresh rook
a city in the north-east of England, on the Tyne

explanation.surface: A chess question about where a lesser promotion lands you.
explanation.walkthrough: Underpromotion is turning a pawn into something other than a queen; a rook is also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a large English city.

clue.text: John's follower, newly sea-sick

indicators.note: sick suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A disciple of John has just become seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: John is John Wesley, founder of Methodism.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wesleyan is a Methodist, a follower of John Wesley.

clue.text: Snare drum played like a soldier

indicators.note: the instrument's name is played around with, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military snare drum is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Under arms means armed and ready for service, as a soldier is.

clue.text: Concerned with minor wound, not in a cast

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a sting is a small wound

explanation.surface: A minor injury that doesn't need a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks medical, but it is the cast of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor between jobs is said to be resting, so not in any cast.

clue.text: Scots community won't admit feminine following

parts.note: to ban is to refuse entry
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A Scottish town refuses entry to women followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Banff is a small town on the coast of north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Batsman being defensive, bowled at chest

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
a locker is a storage chest

explanation.surface: A cricketer playing defensively is bowled by a ball at chest height.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a blocker is a batsman who stonewalls, blocking the ball rather than scoring.

clue.text: Force apple that's for use in the kitchen

definitions.text: that's for use in the kitchen

parts.note: pressure is force applied
a cooker is an apple for cooking rather than eating raw

explanation.surface: Someone pressing an apple meant for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a cooking apple, such as a Bramley, is called a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure cooker is a sealed pan for cooking quickly with steam, a kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Pope departs from African city

indicators.note: the letter for departs is taken from the city

parts.note: Durban is a city in South Africa
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A pope leaves an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is a name taken by several popes.

clue.text: Oriental, contemptible type, raised weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
a fink is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A contemptible eastern figure raises a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: E and FINK make EFINK, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a blade used as a weapon.

clue.text: Pretend embarrassment is not complete

indicators.note: the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: shame is embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be embarrassed but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sham as a verb means to pretend or feign.

clue.text: From sacred island, hard to return to the city

indicators.note: the pieces are turned back, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: Iona is the Hebridean island holy for its early monastery
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A traveller returns from a holy island to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA then H gives IONAH, which read backwards becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Have no desire to join British exclusive arrangement

parts.note: to lack is to have none
list is an old word for desire or wish

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to join an exclusive British club.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacklist is a list of those barred, an arrangement for excluding people.

clue.text: Native hut found in spring wood

indicators.note: the hut is placed inside the month name

parts.note: May is a spring month
a hogan is a traditional Navajo dwelling

explanation.surface: A Native American hut built of wood in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOGAN is the earth-and-timber home of the Navajo people.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown tropical hardwood.

clue.text: Colleague right to interrupt nuisance

indicators.note: the letter for right breaks into the word for nuisance

parts.note: a fiend can be a pest or nuisance

explanation.surface: A colleague is right to break in on an irritating person.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend can be a fellow worker or associate, a colleague.
